Name: e_state
Structural Path: e_state -> execution-state decode -> terminal execution phase -> exec_done
Attack Scenarios: Corrupting e_state can disrupt execution-state decode -> terminal execution phase, delaying or preventing the completion service represented by exec_done.
Justification: Corrupting the execution state prevents or delays a terminal phase, directly suppressing completion service.

Name: frontend_0.decode
Structural Path: frontend_0.decode -> execution launch -> e_state sequencing -> exec_done
Attack Scenarios: Corrupting frontend_0.decode can disrupt execution launch -> e_state sequencing, delaying or preventing the completion service represented by exec_done.
Justification: Decode launches execution; corruption repeatedly prevents legal instructions from reaching completion.

Name: decode_noirq
Structural Path: decode_noirq -> qualified instruction launch -> execution sequencing -> exec_done
Attack Scenarios: Corrupting decode_noirq can disrupt qualified instruction launch -> execution sequencing, delaying or preventing the completion service represented by exec_done.
Justification: This interrupt-qualified decode gate can suppress normal instruction launch and produce sustained completion loss.

Name: frontend_0.e_first_state
Structural Path: frontend_0.e_first_state -> first execution state -> terminal-state progression -> exec_done
Attack Scenarios: Corrupting frontend_0.e_first_state can disrupt first execution state -> terminal-state progression, delaying or preventing the completion service represented by exec_done.
Justification: Incorrect first-state indication disrupts execution entry and subsequent terminal-state selection.

Name: frontend_0.exec_dst_wr
Structural Path: frontend_0.exec_dst_wr -> destination-write phase -> execution completion -> exec_done
Attack Scenarios: Corrupting frontend_0.exec_dst_wr can disrupt destination-write phase -> execution completion, delaying or preventing the completion service represented by exec_done.
Justification: This phase control selects a terminal write state; corruption produces measured stalls and service loss.

Name: frontend_0.exec_src_wr
Structural Path: frontend_0.exec_src_wr -> source-write phase -> execution completion -> exec_done
Attack Scenarios: Corrupting frontend_0.exec_src_wr can disrupt source-write phase -> execution completion, delaying or preventing the completion service represented by exec_done.
Justification: This phase control participates in terminal-state sequencing and can prevent timely completion.

Name: frontend_0.inst_sext_rdy
Structural Path: inst_sext_rdy -> E_SRC_AD transition -> execution progress -> exec_done
Attack Scenarios: Corrupting frontend_0.inst_sext_rdy can disrupt E_SRC_AD transition -> execution progress, delaying or preventing the completion service represented by exec_done.
Justification: Suppressing source-extension readiness strands the FSM in address calculation and prevents completion.

Name: frontend_0.e_state_nxt
Structural Path: frontend_0.e_state_nxt -> e_state register -> terminal-state comparison -> exec_done
Attack Scenarios: Holding e_state_nxt in E_SRC_AD or E_DST_AD, or repeatedly redirecting it away from E_EXEC/E_JUMP/E_DST_WR/E_SRC_WR, prevents timely exec_done assertion.
Justification: This is the value sampled directly into the execution-state register; very-high disruption evidence and an immediate liveness path make it a canonical DoS asset.

Name: frontend_0.exec_jmp
Structural Path: frontend_0.exec_jmp -> exec_done terminal-state mux and E_EXEC/E_DST_WR transitions
Attack Scenarios: A stuck or corrupted exec_jmp changes both the required terminal state for exec_done and the next-state path, potentially preventing the completion condition from being reached.
Justification: exec_jmp is a direct selector in the exec_done equation and a direct execution-FSM transition control; moderate evidence and this strong mechanism justify retention.

Name: frontend_0.inst_dext_en
Structural Path: frontend_0.inst_dext_en/inst_dext_rdy -> E_DST_AD exit condition -> e_state -> exec_done
Attack Scenarios: Suppressing destination-extension readiness can strand the execution FSM in E_DST_AD and prevent it from reaching a terminal exec_done state.
Justification: The canonical candidate contains the inst_dext_rdy alias used directly in the E_DST_AD transition. Its moderate evidence and explicit loop-exit role establish a strong liveness mechanism.

Name: frontend_0.exec_dext_rdy
Structural Path: frontend_0.exec_dext_rdy -> E_DST_AD exit condition -> e_state -> exec_done
Attack Scenarios: Suppressing exec_dext_rdy after a destination extension has been captured can keep E_DST_AD from advancing to E_DST_RD, blocking completion.
Justification: Retained as a narrow-state mechanism override: measured degradation is weak, but exec_dext_rdy is an explicit OR-input to the only exit from E_DST_AD and therefore has a concrete persistent-stall mechanism.
